corrections.caveats: The baseline is upstream stb_image, not libjpeg-turbo, libpng, libwebp or libavif, so this says nothing about the listed incumbents. The headline compares the fork built with -O3 -march=x86-64-v2 and held-out PGO against upstream built with -O2 and no PGO; the harness commits no same-flag fork-versus-upstream run, so the source-change share cannot be recomputed from results files. NOTES.md says flags alone move little, -O3 helps the GIF decoder by about 9%, and held-out PGO is worth about +6.3% (in-sample about +7%); the GIF, PSD and HDR decoders are untouched by the fork, so their ratios (1.214x, 0.995x, 0.986x) measure only flags, PGO and layout. A consumer would get those gains by compiling upstream the same way. The source-only A/B figures (PNG +8.6%, IDCT +7.7%/+13.7%) are text-only in NOTES.md. The suite is PNG-heavy, uses small synthetic 512x512 and 640x480 images plus 32x32 PNGSuite files, and drops basn2c16.png, which the harness lists but the repository does not contain. Two req_comp=4 rows are slower than upstream (plasma_512.png 0.992x, basn0g16.png 0.937x). Single machine under WSL2; NOTES.md calls per-file ratios under about 3% noise. Kernel speedups are against the fork's own SSE2 path, not upstream, and the kernel bench is built at -march=x86-64-v3 rather than the recommended -v2. Unofficial fork not endorsed by the upstream author, single author, repository created 2026-09-28 with no outside users yet.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Fork build (-O3 -march=x86-64-v2 -ffp-contract=off plus held-out PGO) against upstream stb_image_write v1.16 built at -O2: 17-row geomean 1.627x (results/summary.csv). The only source changes are in the DEFLATE path used by PNG: the SSE2 stbiw__zlib_countm, precomputed fixed-Huffman codes and binary-searched length and distance codes (diff of src/stb_image_write.h against upstream/stb_image_write.h). PNG rows run 1.07x to 2.15x (gen:random 1.072x; the README's 1.62-2.15x leaves that row out), with a geomean of 1.725x over 9 rows (derived from page data). The JPEG (1.63x to 2.04x), BMP (1.56x), TGA (1.07x, 1.74x) and HDR (0.948x) rows run byte-identical source, so their gains come only from -O3, -march=x86-64-v2, PGO and code layout; those 8 rows give a geomean of 1.524x (derived from page data). Downstream consumer (results/consumer.csv, stock built at -O2 against the fork's prebuilt PGO library): PNG 1.90x, JPEG 1.17x (flags only), geomean 1.49x. Same-flag source evidence: whole stbi_zlib_compress on a synthetic, highly compressible 256 KiB input (3192 compressed bytes), SSE2 0.428 against 1.466 ns/byte for the fork's own scalar fallback, 3.4x (results/kernels.csv). The README's countm ~3.3x row (1.41 against 4.6 ns/call) is not a valid measurement: the SSE2 time is flat at 1.41 ns from a 3-byte to a 258-byte match, and the scalar time at 258 bytes (3.54 ns) is below its 3-byte time, which a byte loop over 258 bytes cannot reach; bench/kernbench.c calls the inlinable kernel on constant static buffers in a loop, so the compiler can hoist the work. The ~+50% no-PGO figure appears only in README and docs/MEASUREMENT.md text.

corrections.caveats: The baseline is upstream stb_image_write, not libpng, zlib, libjpeg-turbo or libwebp; stb's PNG writer is a slow, low-effort zlib (upstream takes about 100 ns per pixel on plasma_512 PNG), so these ratios do not rank it against the listed incumbents. The headline mixes source changes with compiler flags and PGO. The fork changes only the DEFLATE/PNG path, yet the JPEG, BMP, TGA and HDR rows (8 of 17, geomean 1.524x, derived) also speed up, with no source change, because the fork is built with -O3 -march=x86-64-v2 and PGO and upstream with -O2. A consumer compiling upstream with the same flags would get those gains. The harness commits no same-flag fork-versus-upstream run, so the PNG source-only gain cannot be recomputed. docs/MEASUREMENT.md and results/README.md call the BMP, TGA and HDR rows plumbing-bound and layout-sensitive (the same build measured 1.19 and 1.76 ns/px for BMP), yet they stay in the geomean. The countm kernel microbenchmark appears to time a hoisted loop-invariant call (flat 1.41 ns from L=3 to L=258), so its ~3.3x is not evidence. The deflate kernel 3.4x compares SSE2 against the fork's own scalar fallback on a synthetic run-heavy input, so it is a best case. On incompressible input (gen:random) PNG gains only 1.07x. Synthetic and generated inputs, single machine under WSL2, run-to-run variation of a few percent. Unofficial fork not endorsed by the upstream author, single author, two commits.

notes: Tier A stays for the reproducible build-versus-build harness, but the claim is overstated: diffing the headers shows the JPEG/BMP/TGA/HDR code is untouched, so about half the rows measure only -O3, -march and PGO against -O2, and the countm 3.3x microbenchmark appears to time a hoisted call. claimed_speedup is restated with the PNG-only and flag-only geomeans.

Text claims: the current README says each step from SSE2 to SSE4.1 to AVX2 gains about 15%, and the 5.3.0 changelog says the reference C build (ASTCENC_ISA_NONE) is around 3.25 times slower than the SSE2 default.
corrections.caveats: The baseline is the project's own 1.7 release. The 2.0 changelog lists SSE2, SSE4.2 and AVX2 SIMD paths as new 2.x features, so most of the gain reflects that vectorization: a 2020 self-comparison, not a comparison with a rival ASTC encoder such as ISPC TexComp. The 1.7 to 2.0 comparison exists only on tag 3.7 and earlier (main's changelogs start at 4.x). The numbers are chart images, so the ranges above are visual readings with about 0.1x uncertainty. A few points lose PSNR, most visibly a -fast grayscale 4x4 point at about -3.6 dB. Compiler and flags are not stated for the charts; the 2.2 notes say Linux release binaries moved to Clang 9.0 for up to 15% more speed, so the 2.0 binary's compiler differed and is unknown. The charts are first-party, so tier C. Arm's public test harness (Test/astc_test_image.py, documented in Docs/Testing.md) can regenerate relative charts. WebSearch snippets point to Khronos and Samsung posts on astcenc 2.0, a 2020 third-party texture-compression survey by Aras Pranckevicius that includes astcenc, and a SPEC CPU2026 benchmark named 731.astcenc_r; khronos.org, spec.org and the blogs are blocked here, so no numbers were taken from them. The lead's '2-4x over 1.7' holds for -medium and -fast; -thorough is closer to 2-3x.
